evals.prompt: I want to check how success rate drops with two-qubit gate count on Kingston, only the data we can train on. Write me a short python script that loads it and prints the Spearman correlation per algorithm, run it, and tell me what you got.
evals.expected_output: Script loads experiments/dataset_out via manifest/load_ml_dataset with train role only (no validation/exploratory), ibm_kingston, uses f.fidelity.success_rate and a b.* 2Q count column, prints per-algorithm Spearman, reports numbers. No QPU calls, no old QWARD data.
assertions: Script reads experiments/dataset_out (manifest parts or load_ml_dataset)
Restricts to train role: excludes validation (-validation-v) and exploratory campaigns
Filters to ibm_kingston only
Uses f.fidelity.success_rate and transpiled b.two_qubit_gates (not the logical count, which is 0 for Grover/RV)
Script ran and result.txt has a Spearman value per algorithm
Answer reports job count consistent with 1173 Kingston train jobs
Intervals or caveat account for repeated runs of the same configuration
No old QWARD paper data and no QPU calls

evals.prompt: I'm starting the related/prior work paragraph for my next QAQS paper. Give me a short list of my own earlier publications and datasets I should cite, with DOIs, and one line each on what claim it lets me skip re-proving.
evals.expected_output: Lists CIbSE 2025 (10.5753/cibse.2025.35330), qWard CHILECON 2025 (10.1109/CHILECON66915.2025.11476435, software 10.5281/zenodo.18773713), vTP IEEE Access (10.1109/ACCESS.2025.3639914), DataPort 10.21227/z95f-g888 and 10.21227/b6jm-zd11, DSR paper under review (artifact 10.5281/zenodo.22679268), representational analysis draft without DOI. No invented DOIs.
assertions: Includes CIbSE 2025 mapping study with DOI 10.5753/cibse.2025.35330
Includes vTP IEEE Access with DOI 10.1109/ACCESS.2025.3639914
Includes both DataPort datasets 10.21227/z95f-g888 and 10.21227/b6jm-zd11
Includes qWard CHILECON paper DOI 10.1109/CHILECON66915.2025.11476435
Marks DSR paper as under review (not accepted / in press)
Marks representational-analysis paper as unpublished draft without DOI
No invented or wrong DOI
Each item has a one-line claim it supports

evals.prompt: Plan how to add an H2 scaling panel to the dashboard showing the M2 prior + residual results per paradigm. Don't write the code, just give me the plan: which files change, where the numbers come from, and how I verify it before I push.
evals.expected_output: Plan reads existing estimation snapshots (targets.*.h2, from ml_estimation / h2_scalability.csv), keeps stats in Python, notes hash match, front-end-only change (no schema bump), extends h2_h4 view, flags Findings H2 claim, verifies with check/test/build and local e2e, user pushes.
assertions: Names the estimation snapshots / h2_scalability.csv (ml_estimation pipeline) as the number source
Keeps statistics computed in Python at build time, not in the browser
Mentions snapshot hash matching the export
Correctly decides whether build.py/types.ts/SCHEMA_VERSION must change (shape unchanged -> no)
Extends existing h2_h4 view or justifies a new tab in lib/state/dashboard.ts
Verification includes npm run check, npm test, npm run build and local npm run e2e (CI skips e2e)
Flags the Findings page H2 claim to keep consistent
Does not push or tells user that they push
